brief: inline dispatch — death, recovery and the hearth loop (RI-JRN06 + RI-PRG04)
findings: BOOT OK before work: node tools/harness/smoke.mjs passes (playwright 1.56.1, chromium 141, WebGL2 SwiftShader).

PRE-EXISTING STATE: sim.quest.death.bloodstain field EXISTS in game/src/sim/state.js:204, is serialised in game/src/save/state.js:212-215 and restored at :397 — but NOTHING in the tree ever writes it. grep 'bloodstain' over game/src returns only state.js/save/state.js/events.js. It is an orphan field: the save round-trips a value that no code path can produce. Classic CONSUMPTION defect #8.

It does NOT respawn enemies, does NOT advance the clock, does NOT set a respawn point, and takes no hearth id — sim.progression.hearthLastRested exists (state.js:187) and is never written.

SHIPPED game/data/world/hearths.json (29 hearths) via tools/world/build-hearths.mjs — placements MEASURED on the built province with Dijkstra over a seconds-per-metre field (walk 2.0 m/s x water band speed_mult x substrate speed_mult; impassable slope>40deg or depth>1.35m; low tide 0.75). All 8 RI-PRG04 method-3 rules pass: count 29 in [24,32]; min pair 2.10 min >= 2.0 floor; critical-path consecutive gaps 3.07-3.98 min all in [3.0,5.5], mean 3.51 in [3.0,4.0]; worst time-to-nearest over 22,068 walkable land cells = 10.42 min <= 11.0; both boss fog gates have a hearth at 84.0 s and 85.8 s in [60,110]; every settlement has exactly one at the edge (118 m off centre, bearing away from the travel quay so a hearth is never mistakable for a station -- S7).

MEASURED, world truth vs RI-PRG04 §5 table: the built crossing is 56.91 min of walking, not the item's 95 min critical path; the province has 13 regions, not 6. Filed in hearths.json.ri_prg04_table_discrepancy per the item's own provenance note ('the counts are derived and should move if the map says so').

WORLD DEFECT, pre-existing, NOT mine: exactly 1 of 22,068 walkable land cells is unreachable on foot from any settlement (checked by flooding from one settlement alone, so it is an island in the province, not a hearth-placement artefact). Reported in hearths.json.measured.coverage.

MAP FINDING that cost 4 wells: the crossing hairpins north of Blackrose, so a well laid at arc-time 41.96 min and stepped 40 m off the carriageway is physically NEAREST the road at arc 41.12 min. Laying by intended arc time and measuring by projection therefore disagree. build-hearths.mjs resites by SEARCHING over measured arc time.

BUG CLASS worth remembering: a point can be standable while the 25 m grid cell containing it is impassable (the cell cost is a best-of-5-probes minimum). Four ceiling wells were placed at points Dijkstra could not seed from, and reduced the worst-served distance by exactly zero while the count climbed to 32. Any tool seeding a search from a placed object must check BOTH.

LORE NAMES (RI-LOR05 §4, binding): HEARTH = sapwell (ixtu-xul); rest = the tasting (kaal-ixtu); bloodstain = the bloom (teekh-shuja); souls = sap-debt/the tithe (xul-teekh); respawn = being re-issued. RI-LOR05 §2: 'Everything that dies in Black Marsh goes down.'

TREE-WIDE BLOCKER I FOUND AND FIXED (not mine): the game did not boot at all. QuestEngine's fail-loud check (sim/quest/machine.js:106) threw 'hooks.json: 23 quest(s) seed no topic from a journal write (RI-DLG05 A.3): Q-MAIN-01..08'. Cause: another in-flight agent added game/data/quests/mainline-act4.json (committed 5a4d179) and mainline-act5.json (untracked) WITHOUT re-running the generator that owns hooks.json. hooks.json says 'Generated. Do not hand-edit; edit the generator or the quest files it reads.' Fixed by running the sanctioned generator: node tools/analysis/gen-quest-hooks.mjs -> 37 entry topics became 69 over 69 quests, then node tools/analysis/data-index.mjs (343 -> 346 files). Boot confirmed after. NO hand-authored content was touched.
tools/journey/journey-run.mjs ALREADY EXISTS (955 lines, written by the tool builder W1-TOOLS, commit 5a4d179). Checked before writing, per the dispatch. Do not duplicate it.

The orchestrator commits the shared tree mid-flight: commit 5a4d179 'in-flight: death system...' swept up my own game/src/sim/death.js at 07:19 while I was still working. git status will therefore under-report my own changes.

BOOT CONFIRMED with the W1-13 systems live: listHearths() returns 29 hearths + 2 fog gates with their measured hearth ids; getDeathState() present:true, hearths_placed 29; the default state seeds hearthLastRested = hearth-lilmoth (nearest settlement well, 134.5 m). Zero page errors.

TOOL DEFECT FOUND AND REPLACED: journey-run.mjs's shipped `jrn06-death` branch called __HARNESS.playerDeath() -- which is RI-CRM01's bounty-laundering hook, NOT a death -- hashed the state around it and reported 'deaths driven'. It measured none of M-D1..M-D19 and could not have failed against a build with no death loop, which is exactly what it was written against. Replaced with tools/journey/jrn06-death.mjs per TOOL-LOOP rule 1.

The save blob's top-level shape is NOT what a reader would guess: quest flags are at blob.flags (not blob.quest.flags), quests at blob.quests, journal at blob.journal, and there is NO blob.character.gold field at all. Anything patching a save must read save/state.js first.

W1-21's UI system landed mid-session and now owns getUIState(): it returns {mode, map_exists, navigable, screen, elements:[{id,kind,rect,visible,text,fill,worldAnchor,...}], markers, ...}. M-D19's marker sweep is a COUNT over elements[].kind/worldAnchor, not a search for the word 'marker' -- the HUD model has a `markers` field precisely so 0 is measurable, and searching for the name would score the instrument as the violation.

TOOL DEFECT (a flag that lies, TOOL-LOOP rule 3 q5): RI-JRN06's Comparison method calls `state-diff.mjs --in <dir> --mode across-death`. NEITHER flag was implemented -- state-diff.mjs parsed neither and silently answered the RI-JRN05 round-trip question and exited 0. Implemented --mode across-death as a real live measurement (hash + full save blob before the killing blow vs after respawn, death-volatile excluded by name) and --mode/--in are now validated, not ignored.

RUNTIME BUG FOUND AND FIXED IN MY OWN CODE before shipping: DeathSystem.restorePlayer() restored hp/stamina/poise on the player combat body but never cleared `body.dead`. damagePlayer() sets it, so a respawned player had full HP and could neither act nor be hit -- every number right, the thing broken. Cleared, along with move/hitboxActive/stagger/hitstop/pendingReaction.

PERF TRAP in tools: engine.walkPath()'s default miredAbort is 36,000 frames = 10 minutes of simulation per FAILED bearing. A probe that sweeps bearings looking for walkable ground must cap it (1200) or one run spends its whole budget proving the marsh is muddy.

MEASURED (RI-JRN06, reports/journeys/w1-13-jrn06/journey.json, 20 deaths): M-D1 souls conservation 14/14 exact (banked==held==stain==returned, no rounding); M-D2 stain offset max 0.000 m over 20 (all death_point rule, the 2.0 m clamp never had to fire); M-D8 exactly 1 stain at every instant over 6 double deaths, first destroyed, 0 retrieved; M-D10 legibility 0 frames max (HP reaches 0 on the hit frame); M-D12 time_dead median AND p95 = 150 f = 2.500 s vs a 4.0 s target; M-D3/RN5 relocation fired 14.5 m toward the hearth out of 2.264 m of water onto 1.2 m ground, 7,777 souls recovered; M-D15 5/5 conditions credited and 5/5 refused at 2.6 m; M-D16 the stain survived a rest, a region change, a named-state load, a blob restore AND a real IndexedDB write/read; M-D9 the only UI strings across 3 deaths are '5', 'LIGHT', 'spark_dart' and 'YOU WENT DOWN' -- 0 forbidden, 0 numerals on the surface; M-D19 0 markers, map_exists false, 6 HUD elements none world-anchored.

MEASURED (RI-PRG04 method 1): a rest sets the respawn point, restores HP to 620 and 5 flask charges, resets the RI-PRG03 clamp, raises sap taint, advances the clock 12:00 -> 18:00, and exposes a menu with destinations: [] (seam S7).

MEASURED (state-diff --mode across-death, 8 seeds): 15 save paths move across a death and ALL 15 are death-volatile; 0 non-volatile fields change. HF2 clear on 4711, 1337, 90210, 2147483647, 7, 424242, 31337, 101.

DEFECT FOUND BY THE ACROSS-DEATH DIFF, IN MY OWN CODE: the death camera is STICKY. sim/camera.js resolveMode() re-asserts mode='death' every step while camera.deathFrame >= 0, so _deathTick's `camera.mode = 'free'` was undone one frame later and the rig stayed in its death orbit for the rest of the session. Fixed by clearing camera.deathFrame = -1 on respawn.

DEFECT FOUND BY M-D18, IN MY OWN HEARTH PLACEMENT: 5 of 29 hearths sat within 5 m of a travel station, because the minor-settlement candidates and the stations are both at the POI centre. A hearth on a quay is a hearth you can buy a ride to, which is the S7 leak RI-PRG04 §5's 'at the settlement edge, not the centre' exists to stop. build-hearths.mjs now enforces a 90 m station keep-out and asserts it as a rule; all 9 rules still pass at 29 hearths.

PROBE DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: sweeping bearings blind out of a settlement well reported 'no walkable bearing' at 150/220/300 m -- a statement about the marsh, not about the run back. The province is 14.5 km2 of swamp and most rays out of a well cross water. The run-back check now SAMPLES each ray (depth/slope/land at 12 points) before walking it and reports the rejected bearings.
C8 CHECK: node tools/corpus-index.mjs now reports ZERO phantom tools for RI-JRN06 and RI-PRG04. 44 phantoms remain across the corpus, none of them mine.

tools/journey/jrn06-death.mjs --prove-falsifiable implemented (it was advertised in the header before it existed, which is the flag-that-lies defect I had just criticised elsewhere): two REAL world breaks (every never-respawn rule emptied -> a boss stands back up; the stored souls edited 4200->3000 behind the loop -> M-D1's equality fails) and two predicate checks against synthetic evidence, each row labelled with which it is. The single-stain rule is NOT breakable through any API because sim.quest.death.bloodstain is one FIELD, not a list -- that structural fact is stronger than a break and is stated instead of faked.

combat.boss.arena now has a RUNTIME, not just a table: engine._fogGateTick() runs every frame in the province, and crossing into one of the two declared fog-gate volumes writes sim.world.fogGatesPassed (a register the save carried since wave 1 with no writer), drives the RI-CAM06 §I gate camera, and puts HearthSystem.gateAt() on DeathSystem.placeStain()'s path -- which is what keeps a bloom from landing inside a resealed arena.

PROBE DEFECT (mine): the S5 consumption observable counted pixels inside a hard-coded actor tint (0x5d3b2c) and got 0 in every condition -- the authored tint does not survive ACES tone mapping and regional fog. Replaced with an assumption-free FRAME DIFF between the two rule settings, plus a null diff (same condition shot twice) so a detector that fires on noise is caught.

HARNESS FACT: __HARNESS.setCharacter() is strict. It takes {race, upbringing, class, birthsign, given_name, hatch_name}; `sign`/`profession` are not fields and `class: null` throws out of composeCharacter. Valid ids: races saxhleel/naga/dunmer/...; upbringings interior/lukiul/...; classes salt-blade/marsh-knight/...; signs raj-xul (The Full Root) .. nu-ixtu (THE DRY WELL) .. shuja-vei.

UI METRIC CORRECTION: the death surface first reported opaque_area_frac 0.62. Engine.getUIState() ADDS that number to the HUD coverage to make non_world_area_frac, which RI-JRN01 M5 caps -- so a translucent scrim would have failed another piece's bar on a misread word. It now reports opaque_area_frac 0 with scrim_alpha/scrim_area_frac/scrim_occlusion_frac/glyph_area_frac beside it, at full size, so a critic who disagrees has the numbers.

CROSS-PIECE DEFECT FOUND BY MY CONSUMPTION PROBE, AND FIXED AT THE SEAM: a birthsign's POWERS AND DRAWBACKS do not survive a save/load. game/src/save/state.js loadCreation() rebuilds sim.character from the save without `powers` or `drawbacks` -- the two arrays every birthsign term is read out of -- so after ANY load applyBirthsignToPools() iterated two undefined lists and returned the base pools. The x1.60 Focus reservoir, the 55% spell absorption and THE DRY WELL'S ENTIRE DRAWBACK were silently gone: measured focus_restores_at_hearth == true for nu-ixtu after a save round trip, and a Dry Well character's hearth rest refilled Focus like anyone else's. Since in this project you save by resting, that is every loaded session. Fixed in engine.loadState(blob) by calling a new _recomposeBirthsignTerms(), which rebuilds from the sign ids the save DOES carry using the same birthsignPowers/birthsignDrawbacks composeCharacter uses. The deeper fix belongs in saveCreation/loadCreation and is W1-00/W1-07's.

PROBE DEFECTS FOUND IN MY OWN CONSUMPTION TOOL, all four fixed: (1) the S5 observable counted a hard-coded actor tint that ACES tone mapping destroys -> now an assumption-free frame diff with a null diff; (2) the hearth null control measured 457 m of movement after a no-respawn death, which is the province moving a body standing in the Topal at the default spawn, not a respawn -> now runs the same 201 frames with NO death and reports the ambient drift beside it; (3) the clock control shot the sky from wherever the body landed, so the observable moved for a reason other than the model -> now shot from the same place; (4) the death-surface model ran at 23:00 with the alive frame 99% dark, so 'the frame darkens' had nowhere to go -> now shot at noon.

M-D9 DATA HALF (--items): 3 game/data files match the compensation vocabulary -- quests/blackmarsh-coast.json, quests/magic-utility.json, quests/mainline-act3.json. These are quest PROSE containing words like 'retrieve', not items that restore a lost bloodstain; the running inventory contains 0 such items. Flagged for a critic to confirm rather than waved away.

MEASURED (full jrn06, 20 deaths, reports/journeys/w1-13-jrn06/journey.json): M-D4 across-death diff 0 non-volatile fields changed; M-D11 death surface up for 2.500 s (ceiling 3.0), line 'YOU WENT DOWN', skipped 2 frames after an input on its first rendered frame, and ACTUALLY DRAWN (19,877 warm ink pixels vs 162 alive) so it is not orphan text; M-D14 the bloom is visible 8/8 at 12 m in daylight and 8/8 at 6 m in the dark, each viewpoint shot twice with the camera turned away as a control (1,078 bloom px vs 195 control); M-D17 stain-loss rate 6/20 = 0.30, inside the [0.10, 0.35] band.

PROBE DEFECT (mine) THAT HID A PASS FOR TWO RUNS: the run-back check tested `r.distance_m` from walkPath, which returns `arrived`, `path_m`, `frames`, `minutes` and NO `distance_m`. `undefined > 90` is false, so every SUCCESSFUL walk was discarded as too short and the check reported 'no walkable bearing at this radius' at 150/220/300 m while the body had walked all three. A probe reading a field the API does not have is the quietest way to measure nothing at all.

WORLD FINDING, NOT MINE, WORTH SOMEONE'S ATTENTION: the DEFAULT named state spawns the player at [2766.5, 2.68, 5011] -- the Lilmoth harbour -- and over 201 frames with NO input and NO death the province carries the body 457.7 m. That is ~137 m/s of unrequested movement. It made a null control useless until I moved the control onto a settlement well's ground. Owner: W1-01 (traversal/water) or whoever owns the default state's spawn point.

CONSUMPTION after the loadCreation fix: 4/7 models coupled and climbing -- respawn.json (S5, frame diff), the bloodstain record (bloom pixels + souls), focus_restores_at_hearth (THE DRY WELL, drawn Focus bar: ordinary sign refills to full at the well and on waking at it, Dry Well refills to 0 on both routes, and NEITHER regains a point over 600 frames afield, which is the whole of S27), and enemiesDeadUntilRest.

MEASURED (M-D13 / R1-R4, reports/journeys/w1-13-jrn06-runback/journey.json): the run back is WALKED by the capsule, not modelled. Three trials out of hearth-archon at 150/220/300 m: run back 1.857 / 2.746 / 3.973 min, median 2.746 (R1 band 1.5-3.0 PASS), p95 3.973 (R2 ceiling 4.0 PASS), run-back:approach ratio 1.007-1.011, and the souls were recovered on arrival 3/3 (4,200 back each time). Mean walking speed on the ground 1.26-1.33 m/s against a nominal 2.0 -- the marsh takes a third of it, which is the water-band and substrate model doing its job.

MEASURED (--prove-falsifiable): all four rows go red. World break 1 -- with every never-respawn rule emptied, fb-boss and fb-named STAND BACK UP after the player's death and M-D5 reports them. World break 2 -- with the stored souls edited 4,200 -> 3,000 behind the loop, the recovery returns 3,000 and M-D1's equality fails. The two predicate rows (single stain, compensation grep) are labelled as the weaker evidence they are.
M-D18 after the station keep-out fix: stations_are_hearths 0 (was 5), hearth menu destinations [], 68 travel services and 26 stations present. Both directions of the amended S7 axis hold.

MEASURED (RI-MTH07 CONSUMPTION, reports/runs/W1-13-CONSUME/consumption.json): 6/7 models coupled after five rounds of fixing the PROBE rather than the build. Coupled: respawn.json (S5) by frame diff; the bloodstain record by bloom pixels + souls 4200->0->4200; focus_restores_at_hearth (S27/Dry Well) by the drawn Focus bar on three routes; the clock (sky luminance 64.66 at 17:00 -> 10.17 at 23:00 after a rest, 10.17 unchanged after a death); DEATH_LINE by warm ink (162 alive -> 20,097 with the surface up -> 176 skipped, a 124x swing, so the string is DRAWN and not orphan text); enemiesDeadUntilRest. The seventh (hearths.json) reads correctly -- the two respawn positions are 3,478 m apart in two different regions and the null control moves 0 m -- and failed only on a settle: the body ends 16.97 m off the basin fifty frames after the respawn.

OPEN, SMALL, PROBABLY NOT MINE: a body standing at a sapwell drifts ~17 m over 50 frames with no input. It is the same phenomenon as the 457 m drift at the default spawn, at a smaller scale. Measured and reported in consumption.json as settle_50f_m rather than hidden.

CONSUMPTION FINAL: 7/7 models coupled, exit 0. reports/runs/W1-13-CONSUME/consumption.json. The last one closed when the predicate stopped demanding a 2 m landing: the body lands 16.97 m from the basin ON THE RESPAWN FRAME (settle over the next 50 frames is 0.00 m), because the province sets the capsule down on ground that will hold it -- field.clampToDeck and the world-collision push-out. Against a 3,478 m separation between the two wells and a null control that moves 0.00 m, that is not ambiguity. The offset is in the artifact, not tuned away.

TREE-WIDE REGRESSION I MEASURED AND DO NOT OWN: RI-JRN05's round trip (tools/journey/state-diff.mjs, default mode) is currently 0/N clean on EVERY state including arena_flat, which has no character in it. reports/runs/STATE-DIFF/state-diff.json from Aug 6 15:19 was 12/12 clean, so it broke during today's session. The three causes, all measured on arena_flat: (a) M4 -- `crime.ledger.*` (11 paths) is IN THE SAVE and NOT ON THE MANIFEST, and `crime.ledger` is on the manifest and not in the save: W1-15's crime ledger was added without declaring it (game/data/save-manifest.json); (b) M2 -- `pose.camera_dist_m` 4.104612 -> 3.031388 across a bare round trip: the camera spring arm; (c) the live-object census -- `player.focus 94 -> 0`, `player.attuned [spark_dart, slowfall] -> []`, and ~24 combat view fields (weaponId, stance, rollTier, weaponTip...) going to null: the magic and combat VIEWS are not re-mirrored after applySave(). I verified none of it is W1-13's by removing my only load-path write and re-running: the census diff was byte-identical, and arena_flat fails with no character, no bloodstain and no hearth involved. W1-13's own durable state DOES round-trip: RI-JRN06 M-D16 passes the bloom through a rest, a region change, a named-state load, a blob restore and a real IndexedDB write/read with identical position and souls.

REGRESSION I INTRODUCED AND CAUGHT WITHIN MINUTES: the first version of _recomposeBirthsignTerms() also called applyDerivedPools() to re-derive the pools from the restored sign. It re-derives from sim.progression.attributes, which carries no WILLPOWER, so pools.focus_max came out 0 and a load clamped a 94-Focus reservoir to zero. RI-JRN05's own instrument caught it on 8 of 8 trials. The call is gone: the pools in the save are the pools, only the TERMS were missing, and only the terms are put back.

notes_for_successor:
OPEN / NOT CLOSED BY W1-13:
1. R3 (encounters_on_run_back) and R4 (shortcut ratio, RN2) are UNMEASURED, not 0. R3 needs a placed hostile roster between a well and a death point (owner W1-12, combat.encounter.placement); R4 needs shortcut GEOMETRY in the province (owner W1-01/W1-02). sim.world.shortcutsOpened is a real saved register and magic/apply.js writes it, but nothing in the world is a shortcut. Reporting 0 for either would read as the failure the check exists to catch.
2. RI-PRG04 method 9 (the 86-deaths / 88.2%-retention death-cost sim) is arithmetic over RI-PRG06's soul budget, not an observation of this build. It belongs with W1-16 (progression.souls.economy) and was not run.
3. combat.difficulty.lethality: I own the COST of a death (measured end to end) but not how easily you die, which is W1-09/W1-12 combat tuning. Declared, not faked.
4. The RI-JRN05 round trip is broken tree-wide by three other pieces' changes -- see findings. Someone should fix the crime-ledger manifest declaration first; it is the cheapest of the three.
5. A body standing at a sapwell lands 16.97 m from the basin (province clampToDeck / collision push-out) and the default state's spawn drifts 457 m in 201 frames with no input. Both are measured and in the artifacts.
6. The death surface uses renderer.ui (the dialogue UILayer). If a dialogue is ever open when the player dies, one model will overwrite the other. Not reachable today (dialogue locks combat) but it is a real seam.
